MTCA agreed order (WAC 197-11-268). For SEPA purposes, Ecology determined that reasonable
“bounding” assumptions could be made in Tesoro’s environmental checklist based on the
nature of the presumptive interim actions prescribed in the Agreed Order and facility-specific
information. So long as a future interim action fits within these bounding assumptions, the
assumptions should be sufficient to inform a threshold determination. This approach would not
apply to interim actions that do not implement the presumptive interim actions in the Agreed
Order. In these cases, a separate public notice and SEPA threshold determination will be
required for the work plan submitted to Ecology for approval.
Tesoro submitted an Environmental Checklist for the presumptive actions prescribed in the
Agreed Order. Ecology reviewed the checklist and determined that the proposed action will not
have a probable significant adverse impact on the environment and has issued a Determination
of Nonsignificance.

202105781.proposalName: BP Cherry Point Refinery MS-3/MS-4 Main Substation Upgrade Project
202105781.description:
The proposed project is site preparation and eventual construction of a new electrical substation. The new MS-4 Main Substation, which includes the replacement of the existing MS-3 Substation, will facilitate improved refinery power distribution. The existing MS-3 substation is 34+ years old and contains equipment that is outdated and non-flash arc rated. Installation of the new MS-3/MS-4 substation will allow for redistribution of existing loads and reduce the risk of operating above the safe design limit on existing refinery main substations. Installation of the project will provide improved reliability, safety, and availability and maintainability to the loads it services. PSE will construct a new switchyard and associated infrastructure to feed the new BP substation. BP will coordinate closely with PSE for execution and installation.
The MS-3/MS-4 substation will be situated on an approximately four-acre currently developed site within the existing refinery perimeter. The entire substation site is currently covered with compacted gravel. The existing PSE MS-3 substation equipment will be decommissioned and removed by PSE once the new substation is tested and commissioned.
The completed project will not increase the refinery’s existing maximum crude processing capacity, crude handling at the pier, existing vessel or rail traffic to or from the refinery, or shipment of unrefined fossil fuels that would not be processed or consumed at Cherry Point.

202201096.proposalName: bp Cherry Point Refinery Final Effluent Integrity Management Project- Phase 3, CCTV Camera Pole Installation Project, and West Avenue D Laydown Area
202201096.description:
The BP Cherry Point Refinery (BP) is proposing to construct three separate projects within the existing developed perimeter of the refinery.
Final Effluent Integrity Management (FEIM) Phase 3 Project: The FEIM project will replace the eastern section of the refinery’s existing waste water treatment plant (WWTP) final effluent (treated wastewater) pipe. This section of the effluent line has exceeded its operational design life and requires replacement to eliminate flow capacity deficiencies. The objectives of the project are to restore flow capacity to handle the final effluent from the WWTP during a 25-year, 24-hour duration storm event of 3.5 inches of rainfall, as well as replace the aging pipe.
The project scope includes installation of two parallel 2,270-linear foot, 22-inch HDPE underground pipes to replace the tie-in line to the refinery’s existing emergency wastewater impoundment and the tie-in line to the secondary dock firewater supply line from the refinery firewater header. A temporary construction site access and staging area will be developed at the west end of the alignment, near the intersection of Jackson and Aldergrove Roads. The existing effluent pipe along the Phase 3 Alignment will be abandoned in place.
CCTV Camera Installation Project (CCTV): The purpose of the CCTV project is to install a single CCTV security camera and associated utility pole with pre-cast concrete foundation. The utility pole would be approximately 20 ft. tall. The purposes of the project are to close an existing gap in facility perimeter surveillance and to further satisfy facility and regulatory requirements for refinery security measures.
West Avenue D Laydown Area (WAVE): The project will construct a new gravel laydown area to replace other multi-purpose laydown spaces that have been, or will be, converted to other refinery uses under separate permits. The purpose of the new laydown area is to provide needed space for large equipment and materials storage, construction and turnaround staging, on-going refinery operations and maintenance activities and various non-process related refinery support activities (e.g., welding, painting, fabrication, emergency response). The project scope includes:
- Construction of a 4.2-acre gravel laydown area
- Extension of Avenue D, to the west, to the existing West Brown laydown area gate
- Stormwater management infrastructure modifications and improvements, including extending existing ditches, collecting and routing project site stormwater to the existing West Brown laydown area stormwater treatment and detention pond, and re-routing offsite stormwater around the project site and dispersing it via a new stormwater dispersion trench.
- Site preparation activities consisting of clearing and minor tree cutting, grading, excavation and fill
Per Whatcom County Planning and Development Services request, these projects have been consolidated into one environmental checklist for the purposes of SEPA review. Each of these projects is a standalone proposal that is not functionally or physically connected to the others.
The completed projects will not individually or collectively facilitate improvements that would generate an increase of the refinery’s existing maximum crude processing capacity, crude handling at the pier, existing vessel or rail traffic to or from the refinery, or shipment of unrefined fossil fuels that would not be processed or consumed at Cherry Point.
